investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-28T09:33–09:40Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state, so the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new peer-pod VMs. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent, causing the contract validation to fail completely.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all three probe attempts across a ~7-minute window received the same 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' rejection, indicating sustained exhaustion rather than a transient spike.
[Possible] A prior remote-agent workload (e.g., a long-running or leaked agent VM) is holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and was not cleaned up, leaving zero capacity for new probe pods.

[Possible] The node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes have a hard resource limit on the number of concurrent peer-pod VMs that has been reached.
[Less likely] A cluster scaling event reduced the number of kata-capable nodes from a previously higher count, shrinking available vm slots below the demand level.

[Less likely] The eval runner's withCleanup wrapper (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) failed to release a VM slot from a previous run, contributing to slot exhaustion — though no prior run history is available to confirm this (verifierContext.history.previousRunCount=0).

investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-28 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the remote-agent-state eval produced zero evidence — all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM slots on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no VM capacity remains and preemption cannot help. The eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905), which requires a peer-pod VM; because the pod is stuck unscheduled for ~144s, the agent creation step never completes, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is written, causing the contract validation to fail entirely. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the remote-agent feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

The 4 remaining nodes do not carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource or do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, meaning the schedulable node pool for remote-agent pods is structurally limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size (directly stated in scheduler message).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-28T09:33–09:40Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state, so the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new peer-pod VMs. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent, causing the contract validation to fail completely.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all three probe attempts across a ~7-minute window received the same 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' rejection, indicating sustained exhaustion rather than a transient spike.
[Possible] A prior remote-agent workload (e.g., a long-running or leaked agent VM) is holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and was not cleaned up, leaving zero capacity for new probe pods.

[Possible] The node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes have a hard resource limit on the number of concurrent peer-pod VMs that has been reached.
[Less likely] A cluster scaling event reduced the number of kata-capable nodes from a previously higher count, shrinking available vm slots below the demand level.

[Less likely] The eval runner's withCleanup wrapper (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) failed to release a VM slot from a previous run, contributing to slot exhaustion — though no prior run history is available to confirm this (verifierContext.history.previousRunCount=0).
